description:
About the Position

Amsterdam UMC is recruiting a doctoral candidate (promovendus) for a project on digital, data and AI competencies in healthcare. The project studies which digital, data and AI skills healthcare professionals need, how these competencies can be built into training and continuing education, and how competency development changes practice in clinical settings.

The candidate will run surveys and interviews, analyse training programmes and co-develop educational interventions with clinical and educational partners. The research contributes to national discussions on preparing the healthcare workforce for data-driven care. The appointment is a salaried PhD track under the CAO-UMC collective agreement with a gross monthly salary between EUR 3,217 and EUR 4,077.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in health sciences, educational science, informatics or a related field, with an interest in both healthcare practice and data-driven innovation. Because part of the research takes place in Dutch clinical and educational settings, professional proficiency in Dutch is expected; publications are prepared in English.

Highlights

  • Digital, data and AI competencies in healthcare
  • Training and continuing-education research
  • Survey, interview and intervention studies
  • Healthcare workforce development
  • Co-design with clinical and educational partners
  • Salaried PhD, EUR 3,217 - 4,077 per month (CAO-UMC)

About Amsterdam UMC

Amsterdam UMC is the combined academic medical centre of the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, operating from AMC and VUmc campuses. It is one of the largest biomedical research institutions in the Netherlands, with research programmes spanning infectious diseases, oncology, cardiovascular science, epidemiology, public health and health data science. The centre employs PhD candidates and postdocs on salaried contracts under the CAO-UMC collective agreement. Research vacancies are published on the werkenbij.amsterdamumc.org portal, and many doctoral projects are embedded in national and European research consortia.
